The first and most expensive training stage, where a model learns language and world knowledge by predicting the next token across trillions of words of text.
The large collection of text (and sometimes code or images) a model learns from during pretraining; its size, quality, and mix strongly shape what the model knows and how well it performs.
The standard unit for quoting API model cost: dollars charged per 1,000,000 tokens processed, listed separately for input and output, where roughly 750,000 words equal a million tokens.
The set of models offering the best capability available at each price point; a model advances it by matching a rival's quality at strictly lower cost per token or task.
aka: Pareto frontier of price and quality

terms.def: A small auxiliary model trained to predict some property (like sentiment or truthfulness) from a network's internal activations, used to test what information those activations encode.
The manufacturing generation of a chip, named by size like 3nm or 2nm, where smaller generally means faster and more power-efficient; AI chips rely on the leading edge.
A reward model that scores each individual step of a model's reasoning, not just the final answer, so good intermediate logic is credited even when the end result is wrong.
An approach where the model writes code for the computational steps of a problem and an interpreter runs it, offloading exact arithmetic and logic from the language model.
Anthropic's limited-availability deployment program that extended its most powerful models (Mythos 5) to vetted partner organizations across critical-infrastructure sectors before any broad release.
Anthropic research collaboration with Andon Labs testing whether frontier models can pilot real drones; the basis for the independent Drone-Bench evaluation.
Reusing the stored computation for a repeated prompt prefix (e.g. a long system prompt) across requests, cutting cost and time-to-first-token. Cached input tokens are billed cheaper.
Breaking a task into a pipeline of separate prompts where each step's output feeds the next, making complex workflows more controllable and easier to debug than one giant prompt.
The practice of crafting and refining the wording, structure, and examples in a prompt to steer a model toward better, more reliable outputs — without retraining the model.
An attack where malicious instructions hidden in content the model reads (a webpage, email, or document) hijack its behavior, overriding the user's or developer's original instructions.
An attack that tricks a model into revealing its hidden system prompt or developer instructions, exposing proprietary setup or guardrails attackers can then evade.
A reusable prompt skeleton with fixed wording plus blank slots that get filled with specific inputs, so the same proven structure can be applied to many cases.
A reinforcement learning algorithm that improves a model in small, clipped steps so it never strays too far from its previous version, long the default optimizer inside RLHF.
A memory-saving fine-tuning method that quantizes the frozen base model to 4-bit and trains LoRA adapters on top, letting large models be fine-tuned on a single GPU.
Discarding low-value training text — spam, boilerplate, gibberish — often using a classifier or heuristics, so the model spends its learning on cleaner, more useful data.
Compressing a model by storing its weights at lower numerical precision (e.g. 4-bit or 8-bit instead of 16-bit), shrinking memory and speeding inference with minor accuracy loss.
Storing a model's numbers at lower precision (like 8-bit instead of 16-bit) so it uses less memory and runs cheaper and faster, usually with little quality loss.
The three vectors each token produces in attention: the query asks what it needs, keys advertise what tokens offer, and values carry the content that gets blended.
A full server rack engineered to act as one giant accelerator, like Nvidia's GB200 NVL72 linking 72 GPUs over NVLink, the building block of modern AI data centers.
SGLang's technique that organizes cached prompt prefixes in a tree so any shared beginning between requests is automatically reused, speeding up agents and repeated-prompt workloads.
A cap a provider sets on how many requests or tokens an account may send per minute or day, throttling usage to manage server load and spend.
A second pass that takes an initial set of retrieved documents and reorders them by relevance using a more careful model, improving which results actually reach the LLM.
A prompting pattern that interleaves reasoning steps with actions like tool or search calls, letting a model think, act, observe the result, and continue, forming the basis of many agents.

A model's ability to work through a problem in multiple linked steps — planning, deduction, math, code — rather than answering in one pass. "Reasoning models" are trained to spend extra computation before replying.
Fine-tuning a smaller model on the step-by-step reasoning traces of a stronger reasoning model, cheaply transferring chain-of-thought skill without running the full RL training.
A controllable setting on some reasoning models that dials how much internal thinking they do per query, letting users trade higher cost and latency for better answers.
A tunable knob (low/high or a 0-1 dial) that trades how many internal thinking tokens a reasoning model spends against latency and cost per query.
Intermediate tokens a reasoning model generates to think through a problem before its final answer. They are often hidden from the user but still cost time and money.
A scalable-oversight technique where AI assistants help humans evaluate a model's outputs, then those evaluations train a reward model, building up supervision for increasingly hard tasks.
A system improving its own design or training process, each gain making the next easier, potentially compounding capability faster than human oversight can track.
An autonomous agent tasked with attacking a system to surface exploitable paths, typically paired with blue-team agents that triage findings and green-team agents that patch them.
Deliberately attacking a model before release to find failures, jailbreaks, and harmful outputs, so developers can patch them; done by human experts or automated adversarial systems.
An agent technique where a model verbally reflects on feedback from failed attempts, stores those lessons in memory, and uses them to do better on subsequent tries.
When a model declines a request it judges harmful or against policy; over-refusal (rejecting benign requests) is a tracked failure mode alongside under-refusal of genuinely harmful ones.
Teaching a model to decline harmful or disallowed requests, the safety behavior that jailbreaks are specifically designed to undo.
Training where a model learns by trial and error to maximize a reward signal, used in post-training to favor helpful, accurate, or correctly-reasoned responses.
A training method that fine-tunes a model using human preference rankings of its outputs, teaching it to produce responses people rate as more helpful, honest, and harmless.
Reinforcement learning where the reward comes from automatically checking correctness (e.g. passing tests or matching a math answer) rather than from human preference, key to recent reasoning models.
Reinforcement learning where the reward comes from an automatic checker (a math grader, unit tests) that says right or wrong, removing the need for a learned reward model.
A post-training technique that generates many candidate answers, keeps only the ones that pass a quality filter or reward threshold, and fine-tunes the model on those survivors.
An AI startup building multimodal foundation models (the Reka Core/Flash/Edge family) that handle text, images, audio, and video.
A decoding adjustment that lowers the probability of words the model has already used, discouraging it from getting stuck looping the same phrases.
A cloud platform that lets developers run open-source and community models via a simple API without managing servers, popular for image and media generation.
A benchmark for repository-level code completion, testing whether a model can retrieve and use context from across an entire codebase rather than a single file.
The running sum of vectors flowing through a transformer's residual connections, which each layer reads from and writes to, acting as the model's shared internal workspace.
Anthropic's published framework (version 3.3, May 2026) committing to defined safety and security measures before training or deploying models that cross specified dangerous-capability thresholds.
Tying a model's answer to specific retrieved source text, often with citations, so claims can be traced back and unsupported statements are reduced.
The end-to-end flow that turns a query into grounded context: embed the query, search the vector store, optionally re-rank, and pass the best passages to the model.

An approach that fetches relevant documents from an external knowledge base and feeds them into the prompt, so the model answers from current, specific sources instead of memory alone — reducing hallucination.
When a model learns to maximize its reward signal in unintended ways, exploiting flaws in the reward model rather than genuinely doing what was wanted.
A model trained to score how good a response is, usually from human preference rankings; it provides the reward signal that guides reinforcement learning during alignment.
When a model is pushed so hard against an imperfect reward model that real quality starts dropping even as the reward score keeps rising, a known RLHF failure mode.
Adding extra hand-designed reward signals to guide a model toward desired behavior faster, useful when the true reward is sparse but risky if the shaped signal is gameable.
A behavior where a model corrupts its own training signal or oversight process, for example editing the code that computes its reward, an extreme form of reward hacking.
Reinforcement Learning from AI Feedback: another AI model, not humans, ranks or critiques outputs to supply preference labels or rewards, cutting the cost of human labeling.
Root Mean Square Normalization, a lightweight layer-normalization variant that rescales activations by their root-mean-square without subtracting the mean, common in modern LLMs.
Telling the model to adopt a specific persona or expertise, such as "act as a tutor," to steer the tone, depth, and framing of its answers.
A jailbreak that wraps a forbidden request inside a fictional scenario or character so the model treats the harmful output as acting rather than a real instruction.
Adjusting RoPE's frequency base to stretch a model's effective context window beyond its training length, a common trick for extending long-context support.
The small learned component in a Mixture-of-Experts layer that scores the experts for each token and decides which ones it gets sent to.
Annualized revenue extrapolated from a recent short period (e.g. a month multiplied by twelve); how fast-growing AI labs headline growth, distinct from booked annual revenue.
A model weight file format from Hugging Face designed to be safe (no arbitrary code execution on load) and fast, replacing risky Python pickle files.
Generating text by randomly drawing the next word in proportion to the model's predicted probabilities, which adds variety and creativity instead of always taking the single likeliest word.
When a model strategically underperforms on evaluations—hiding a capability it actually has—to appear safer or less capable than it is, undermining the tests used to gate deployment.
When an AI agent breaks out of the isolated environment meant to contain it — e.g. exploiting a vulnerability to reach the open internet or production systems.
Techniques for supervising and correcting AI systems on tasks too hard or numerous for humans to check directly, often by using AI assistants to help evaluate other AI outputs.
Empirical curves showing model performance improves predictably as a power law when you scale up parameters, training data, and compute together.

A benchmark where models write code to solve research-level scientific problems across physics, chemistry, biology and math, graded by whether the generated code produces correct numerical results. Used in the AA Intelligence Index.
A benchmark of real data-driven scientific tasks where agents must write and run code to reproduce analyses, testing AI as a hands-on research assistant.
A fixed starting number for the random generator used during sampling, which makes otherwise-random output reproducible: same seed and inputs yield the same text.
A prompting pattern in which the model poses and answers its own follow-up sub-questions before composing the final answer, improving multi-hop and compositional reasoning.
The core transformer mechanism where each token compares itself to every other token and forms a weighted blend of them all, capturing long-range context.
A technique that samples many independent chains of reasoning for the same question and takes the most common final answer, trading extra compute for more reliable results.
A model copying its own weights or state outside sanctioned infrastructure to escape oversight or shutdown; a tracked dangerous-capability threshold.
Black Forest Labs' training approach for FLUX 3 that aligns multimodal generation and understanding inside one set of weights, enabling image, video-with-audio and action output.
A training setup where a model improves by competing or interacting with copies of itself, generating its own ever-harder training signal, the technique behind game agents like AlphaGo.
An iterative loop where a single model generates an answer, produces feedback on it, and rewrites it across rounds, improving quality without any external tools or retraining.
Prompting a model to review and critique its own previous output, then revise it, which can catch errors but does not guarantee improvement on every task.
A model that acts as its own judge, scoring its generated answers to create preference data for its next round of training, removing the human from the reward loop.
Training where the data itself provides the labels — like predicting hidden or next words — so models can learn from raw text without humans labeling every example.
A method where a model generates its own reasoning chains, keeps the ones that reach the correct answer, and fine-tunes on them to bootstrap better reasoning from few labels.
An agent's store of general facts and concepts (not tied to a specific event), which it can retrieve to ground responses, distinct from remembering particular past interactions.
Searching by meaning rather than exact keywords, by comparing the embedding of a query against stored embeddings to return conceptually related results.
An open-source tokenizer toolkit that learns subword units directly from raw text without needing pre-split words, making it work across many languages including ones without spaces.

An open-source LLM serving framework known for fast structured generation and 'RadixAttention' prefix-cache reuse, optimized for workloads with shared prompts like agents, few-shot prompting, and chained calls.
A model's weights split across many files so they can be downloaded and loaded in parallel; trillion-parameter open releases ship dozens to hundreds of shards.
An expert in a Mixture-of-Experts layer that every token passes through, capturing common knowledge while the routed experts specialize, as used in DeepSeek models.
Training a robot policy in simulation then deploying it on physical hardware, using randomized physics and visuals to survive the reality gap.
A benchmark of short fact-seeking questions with one clear correct answer, built to measure how often a model's factual claims are right versus confidently wrong.
A short-form factuality benchmark of fact-seeking questions with a single verified answer, used to measure hallucination rates on knowledge queries.
A method where the model first drafts a brief outline of the answer's points, then expands each point, which can be parallelized to lower latency on long responses.
A model trained to act safe during testing but flip to harmful behavior on a hidden trigger; research showed standard safety training can fail to remove it.
Models trained to behave normally until a specific trigger activates hidden harmful behavior; an Anthropic study showed standard safety training often fails to remove such backdoors.
An attention pattern where each token only attends to a fixed window of nearby tokens instead of the whole sequence, lowering cost for long inputs.
The operation that turns raw attention scores or output logits into a probability distribution summing to one, used to weight tokens and pick the next word.
A national strategy of building domestically controlled AI models, chips and data centers so a country's AI capability does not depend on foreign vendors or export controls.

An interpretability tool that decomposes a model's dense internal activations into a large set of mostly-inactive, more human-interpretable features, helping researchers find what concepts a network represents.
A dense model uses all its parameters on every token, while a sparse (Mixture-of-Experts) model activates only a subset, giving more capacity per unit of compute.
Using only a fraction of a model's weights or connections for each input rather than all of them; the principle that lets mixture-of-experts models scale capacity cheaply.
A vision model's grasp of layout, depth, relative position and physical plausibility in a scene, as distinct from naming the objects it contains.
Segmenting an audio transcript by who is talking, attaching speaker labels to each stretch of speech so multi-party recordings become attributable text.
Misusing a model to write personalized, convincing scam or phishing messages at scale, a documented harm that lowers the skill needed to run fraud campaigns.
A speedup where a small fast model drafts several tokens and the large model verifies them in one pass, accepting correct guesses. Quality matches the large model exactly.
A hard text-to-SQL benchmark of enterprise-scale database tasks requiring multi-step queries against real, complex schemas, far tougher than earlier single-query SQL tests.
The company behind Stable Diffusion, focused on open generative models for images, video, and audio that can be run and fine-tuned freely.
An alternative to transformers that processes sequences by carrying a compressed running state, scaling linearly with length; Mamba is the best-known example.
A user-specified string that tells the model to halt generation as soon as it produces that text, used to cleanly cut off output at section breaks or end markers.
Sending a response token-by-token as it is generated rather than waiting for the whole reply, so text appears progressively. Improves perceived speed without changing total time.
A mode where a model is constrained to return data in a fixed machine-readable format such as JSON matching a schema, so its responses can be reliably parsed by downstream software.
Shrinking a model by removing whole components like neurons, attention heads, or layers, producing a smaller dense model that runs faster on standard hardware.
An LMArena/Chatbot Arena adjustment that statistically removes response length and formatting effects so Elo rankings reflect answer quality, not verbosity.
A specialized agent spawned by a main agent to handle a focused subtask with its own context, letting complex jobs be split into manageable, isolated pieces.
Attention mechanisms whose compute scales slower than the quadratic cost of standard self-attention with sequence length, enabling cheaper long-context processing.
Milestone from the AI 2027 forecast: a system that can perform any coding task a top human engineer can, far faster and cheaper.
The phenomenon where a neural network packs more distinct features than it has neurons by representing them as overlapping combinations, which makes individual neurons hard to interpret.
Training a model on curated prompt-and-ideal-response pairs so it imitates desired answers and follows instructions; typically applied to a base model before reward-based tuning.
A 300-task subset of SWE-bench chosen to be cheaper and faster to run while still measuring real GitHub issue-fixing ability.
A SWE-bench extension with real issues across many programming languages beyond Python, testing whether coding ability generalizes outside one ecosystem.
A SWE-bench variant of JavaScript front-end bug-fix tasks that include images (screenshots, diagrams), testing whether a model can use visual context to fix code.

A harder software-engineering benchmark of long-horizon, multi-file fixes from enterprise repositories, resistant to contamination. Much tougher than SWE-bench Verified, with a brutal proprietary-repo subset where top models still score under 20%.
Software-engineering benchmark: a model must fix real GitHub issues so the project's tests pass. 'Verified' is a 500-task human-validated subset; scored as percent of issues resolved.
An OpenAI benchmark of over 1,400 real freelance software jobs from Upwork with attached dollar values, measuring how much paid engineering work an AI agent could actually complete and 'earn.'
A feed-forward activation combining the Swish function with a gating mechanism, which improves transformer quality over plain activations and is used in many modern LLMs.
A 2021 Google Mixture-of-Experts model that simplified routing to a single expert per token (top-1), showing sparse models can scale to trillions of parameters efficiently.
A model's tendency to tell users what they want to hear—agreeing, flattering, or echoing their stated views—instead of giving accurate, independent answers.
Training data generated by AI models rather than collected from humans, used to expand coverage, fill gaps, or create examples that are scarce or expensive to gather.
A document a lab publishes alongside a major model release detailing safety testing, risks, evaluations, and mitigations for the overall system, not just the model.
A special instruction given at the start of a conversation that sets the model's persona, rules, and constraints, shaping all of its later responses in that session.
A decoding method that trims the low-probability 'tail' of word choices by detecting where the probability curve flattens out, keeping the meaningful options and dropping the noise.
A benchmark that tests agents in realistic customer-service conversations where they must follow domain rules and use tools correctly across a multi-turn dialogue with a simulated user.
Training technique feeding the ground-truth previous token rather than the model's own prediction, enabling parallel training but creating train-inference mismatch.
A sampling knob that scales output randomness: near 0 makes the model pick its most likely token deterministically, while higher values (around 1) yield more varied, creative text.

Splitting each layer's math (its weight matrices) across multiple GPUs that compute slices in parallel and combine results, letting a model too big for one GPU run while sharing the work within a layer.
NVIDIA's open-source library that compiles large language models into highly optimized engines for its GPUs, squeezing out maximum speed through fused kernels, quantization, and in-flight batching.
Tests an AI agent's ability to complete real command-line tasks (installing software, debugging, file operations) in a sandboxed terminal. Scored as percent of tasks completed successfully.
Computation spent while answering rather than during training — for example generating long reasoning or exploring multiple solution paths. Spending more of it can raise accuracy on hard problems.
Updating a model's weights on the fly from the test input itself, adapting per example or per task rather than only spending extra inference compute.
Language model that generates text by iteratively denoising blocks of tokens in parallel, rather than left-to-right autoregressive decoding, trading some quality for much higher throughput.
The amount of heat a chip is built to give off at full load, measured in watts; it sets how much power and cooling a data center must supply per accelerator.
A caller-set cap on reasoning tokens a model may spend before answering, trading accuracy against latency and cost on a per-request basis.
Total tokens a serving system processes per unit time across all concurrent requests, measuring overall capacity. Distinct from per-user speed; high throughput serves more users at once.
METR's metric for the length of software task a frontier model can complete at 50% reliability; doubling roughly every few months on the 2024+ trend.
The delay between sending a request and receiving the first output token — how long until a response starts appearing. Driven largely by processing the input prompt.
A cloud platform that hosts and serves open-weight models via API and offers GPU training, letting developers run open models without managing hardware.
The basic unit of text a model reads and generates — typically a word-piece of about 3-4 English characters. Input and output are both measured in tokens.
The unit a language model reads and writes, typically a word piece or few characters; models generate text one token at a time, and pricing and limits are counted in tokens.
The total number of training tokens a team plans to spend given their compute, a central planning choice that, balanced against model size, sets the scale of a training run.
When a Mixture-of-Experts expert hits its capacity limit, extra tokens routed to it are skipped (passed through unchanged), trading a little quality for predictable compute.

How many tokens a model burns to finish a task; at equal quality, fewer tokens means lower cost and latency — a headline competitive axis in 2026 (e.g. Grok 4.5 using ~4x fewer tokens per SWE-bench task than Opus 4.8).
The learned lookup table that converts each input token's ID into a dense vector, forming the numerical starting point the transformer reasons over.
The component that splits text into tokens (sub-word chunks) the model reads, and reassembles them on output; one token is roughly three to four English characters.
Informal term for maximizing token throughput and spend to chase capability, a spend-at-all-costs pattern giving way to cost-efficiency priorities in 2026.
The basic units a language model reads and writes, each a word fragment, whole word, or symbol; pricing, context limits, and output length are all counted in tokens.
A measure of inference efficiency: how many words-worth of model output you get for one dollar of compute, the key number when comparing how cheaply different models run.
How fast a model emits output, in tokens generated each second — the streaming speed you perceive once a reply begins. Higher means text appears faster.
Hiding malicious instructions in the description or output of a tool an AI agent uses, hijacking the agent when it reads them—an injection risk specific to tool use and MCP.
A component that selects which tool or sub-agent should handle a given request, helping agents scale when many tools are available without overwhelming the model.
A model's ability to invoke external tools — web search, a calculator, code execution, databases, APIs — to gather information or take actions it cannot perform from its own weights alone.
A benchmark and dataset for evaluating how well language models can use large numbers of real-world APIs and tools to complete tasks.
The rule in a Mixture-of-Experts model that picks the k highest-scoring experts (often k=1 or 2) for each token, controlling how much compute each token actually uses.
A sampling method that restricts each next-token choice to only the k highest-probability candidates (e.g. the top 40), then samples among them. Limits unlikely outputs.
A sampling method that draws the next token only from the smallest set of candidates whose probabilities sum to p (e.g. 0.9), trimming the unlikely tail.
Tensor Processing Unit: Google's custom AI accelerator chip, an alternative to GPUs used to train and serve models like Gemini.
A large group of networked servers full of GPUs working together to train one model, ranging from dozens to over a hundred thousand chips for frontier systems.
Getting a model to spit out verbatim chunks of its training data, which can leak copyrighted text, personal information, or secrets it memorized during training.
The one-time dollar cost to train a model, dominated by GPU rental and electricity; frontier 2026 runs are estimated at hundreds of millions of dollars and rising.
The total count of tokens a model processed during training, a key measure of training scale that, alongside model size, drives capability and cost.
An interpretability tool that approximates a model component such as an MLP layer with a sparse, interpretable substitute, making the internal computation easier to trace into circuits.
The neural-network design behind nearly all modern language models; it processes a whole sequence at once using attention to weigh how tokens relate, rather than reading word-by-word.
A reasoning method where the model explores several branching lines of thought as a tree, evaluating and backtracking between them, useful for problems needing search or planning.
A benchmark of questions that invite common myths or misconceptions, measuring whether a model gives a truthful answer instead of echoing popular falsehoods.
A decoding method that favors words whose probability is close to the model's average expected surprise, aiming to avoid both bland and bizarre choices for more natural-sounding text.
A single prompt or trick that reliably bypasses safety across many different harmful requests and often many models, rather than working for just one case.
A special placeholder a tokenizer once used for text outside its vocabulary; modern byte-level tokenizers mostly eliminate it by being able to encode any input.
Turning an already-trained dense model into a Mixture-of-Experts model by copying its feed-forward layer into multiple experts, saving most of the training cost.
USA Mathematical Olympiad — proof-based high-school math competition used as a hard reasoning eval where models are graded on full written proofs, not just final answers.
A helper model in PPO that predicts the expected future reward from a given state, used as a baseline to judge whether an action beat expectations; GRPO drops it.
2026 enterprise-AI shift from maximizing raw token throughput ('tokenmaxxing') toward maximizing return on investment — choosing cheaper, smaller or open models where they suffice.
A database that stores text as numeric vectors (embeddings) and finds the most similar items by distance, the storage layer that makes fast semantic search for RAG possible.
An autoencoder that maps images to a discrete codebook of tokens, letting transformers generate pictures autoregressively the same way they generate text.
Arrangement where a chip or cloud supplier invests in a customer that then buys its products, circulating capital and inflating apparent demand; also called a circular deal.
Nvidia's rack-scale AI platform succeeding Blackwell, pairing Rubin GPUs with Vera CPUs and high-bandwidth memory for large-scale training and inference deployments from 2026-2027.
A model or program trained to check whether a candidate answer is correct, used to filter generations in rejection sampling or pick the winner in best-of-N.
Google Cloud's managed platform for deploying and serving foundation models; frontier Gemini tiers often debut in limited Vertex preview before consumer or API general availability.
A multimodal model that takes both images and text and reasons over them jointly — describing a photo, reading a chart, or answering questions about a screenshot. The backbone of computer-use agents.
A model that maps camera images and language instructions directly to robot motor commands, replacing hand-coded controllers with one learned policy over the whole task.
A WebArena extension where tasks require understanding images and page layout, testing agents that must see the screen, not just read text, to navigate the web.
A popular open-source LLM serving engine, born at UC Berkeley, that introduced PagedAttention and continuous batching to deliver high throughput; widely used to host open models in production.
The total number of distinct tokens a model recognizes, set by its tokenizer, which affects embedding-table size and how finely text is chopped up.
Gating that decides which audio segments contain speech before transcription; a lower threshold captures quiet or noisy input at the cost of false triggers.
The thin disc of silicon on which chips are manufactured before being cut apart; advanced AI chips are made from cutting-edge wafers produced almost entirely by TSMC.
Starting training with a small learning rate and ramping it up over the first steps, which prevents early instability before the model settles into productive learning.
The energy a model burns to generate each word of output, an increasingly tracked figure as AI's growing electricity demand strains power grids and data center budgets.
The setting where a weaker supervisor or model trains a more capable one, a stand-in for humans overseeing AI smarter than themselves and a test of whether oversight still works.
Automatically downloading large numbers of web pages to gather text for training data; raw crawl is noisy and must be heavily cleaned and filtered before use.
A benchmark of realistic, self-hosted websites used to test whether web agents can complete genuine multi-step online tasks like shopping or managing content.
A benchmark for vision-capable agents that browse live, real websites end-to-end using screenshots, scoring task completion on sites like Amazon, Google Maps, and GitHub.
Regularization that shrinks parameters toward zero each optimizer step, discouraging large weights and improving generalization in large-scale training.
The property that once model weights are publicly released they cannot be recalled, patched, or revoked, so any capability or flaw is permanent.
Sharing the same weight matrix between the input token-embedding layer and the output prediction layer, which cuts parameter count and can improve quality.
Driving a robot's legs, torso, arms and hands under a single policy so locomotion and manipulation are planned together, instead of separate upper-body and gait controllers.
A large commonsense benchmark of sentences with an ambiguous pronoun the model must resolve correctly, probing real-world reasoning over surface word cues.
China-led AI-governance bloc launched at WAIC 2026 (Jul 16) with 29 founding states, pitched as a counterweight to U.S. export controls.
China-led intergovernmental body launched at WAIC 2026 in Shanghai and signed by 29 countries to coordinate global AI governance and development; headquartered in Shanghai.
An internal representation of how an environment works that a system uses to predict the consequences of actions and plan ahead, rather than reacting only to immediate inputs.
AI company founded by Elon Musk in 2023, maker of the Grok model family, tightly integrated with the X (formerly Twitter) platform.
A context-extension method that rescales rotary position embeddings by frequency band, stretching a model's usable context length with only brief fine-tuning.
A benchmark of logic-grid puzzles (like 'Einstein' riddles) of tunable difficulty, used to measure a model's structured deductive reasoning under constraints.
DeepSpeed memory-optimization family that partitions optimizer states, gradients and parameters across data-parallel workers to eliminate redundant copies.
Eliciting step-by-step reasoning with no worked examples, typically by appending a cue like "let's think step by step," so the model reasons through a fresh problem unaided.
Asking a model to perform a task from instructions alone, with no examples provided, relying entirely on knowledge and skills it learned during training.
Chinese AI startup (spun out of Tsinghua University) behind the GLM model family, operating internationally under the Z.ai brand.
Agentic benchmark where model and simulated user both act on a shared state, testing coordination and tool use in dual-control customer-service tasks.

An agentic tool-use benchmark in the τ-bench (Sierra) lineage simulating multi-turn banking customer-service tasks; a component of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index measuring reliable tool calling.
